**Procedure:** Access Review Procedure · **Window:** planned Sep 21 to Sep 30 · **Status (Oct 9):** 14 of 20 systems signed off (70%). Late; exception to be documented. Target completion 2026-10-10.

## Findings so far

- 21 accounts removed, 4 reduced, across 14 systems.
- One local (non-SSO) account found: a Pillar Bank portal login created for the ACH cut-over shadow period and never removed. Removed Oct 1.
- GitHub: 3 former contractors still in the org with read access to the monolith. Removed. Offboarding workflow didn't cover GitHub outside collaborators; fixed.
- Postgres: one engineer had direct production write access left over from the cut-over. Reduced to read via the on-call role.
- No evidence of access by anyone who shouldn't have had it.

## Why it's late

- Nine of the twenty systems are owned by Marcus Bell, who spent late September on the Sep 26 incident and the Pillar follow-up.
- Devon Park owns Snowflake and is heads-down on the reconciliation fix for investing GA.
- I started the window on Sep 21 instead of Sep 1. That's on me; the procedure says the whole last month.

Risk: the Type II auditor will sample Q3 and see the late completion. Documented with cause and a plan, that's an exception, not a failure. Two late quarters in a row would be a pattern.

Decision: the Q4 review starts 2026-12-01, and Tier 1 systems go first so the riskiest ones are never the late ones.
